comparator.name: University College Maastricht (Liberal Arts and Sciences)
comparator.academicYear: 2026-2027 (Education and Examination Regulations 2026-2027, Maastricht School of Liberal Arts and Sciences, UCM programme, in force 1 September 2026; programme pages checked 2026-10-02)
comparator.sourceNotes: The programme pages (s1, s2, s3) describe the structure only in words: an academic core, two to four general education courses, a concentration in the social sciences, humanities or sciences (or an interdisciplinary mix), skills trainings, three-week projects and a Capstone. They give no EC, and the 'View current courses' catalogue is not readable from this environment (the 2024-2025 curriculum PDF is blank). The 180-EC reconstruction therefore follows the 2026-2027 Education and Examination Regulations of the Maastricht School of Liberal Arts and Sciences (s0, UCM programme; in force 1 September 2026): Article 3.6 (180 EC), 3.7 (components), 3.8 (core of four 5-EC courses plus core skills trainings and projects of 20 EC for UCM, and 10-20 EC of general education), 3.9 (concentration of 14-16 courses and 70-80 EC, six skills trainings of 15 EC, three projects of 15 EC, and a 20-EC Capstone) and Appendix I (named core courses COR1002, COR1003, COR1004, COR1007; core skills trainings SKI1008, SKI1004, SKI1005; core projects PRO1014 of 7.5 EC and PRO1012 of 5 EC). The regulations do not state the credit value of each core skills training; 2.5 EC each follows from the 20-EC core skills-and-projects total (20 minus 7.5 and 5 leaves 7.5 EC for three skills trainings) and from the 2.5 EC per skills training in Article 3.9(4). Fixed components total 90 EC (core courses 20, core skills and projects 20, concentration skills 15, projects 15, Capstone 20); the remaining 90 EC are general education plus concentration courses, where the regulations allow 10-20 and 70-80 EC. I instantiated the midpoint (3 general education courses, 15 EC; 15 concentration courses, 75 EC), which is valid. The concentration domain, its courses, the general education courses and the choice of skills trainings and projects are individual student choices that the official sources do not fix, so they are kept as explicit restricted-choice components without invented course names. Article 3.9(11) also permits an interdisciplinary concentration, which does not change the 180-EC structure. Checked 2026-10-02. A human may wish to confirm the core skills-training credits and the 15/75 split against the UCM course catalogue.

Research Methods II (SKI1005, core skills training)

courses: New Issues in Contemporary Social Theory

core: Academic core: the four core topics every UCM student studies, namely how scientific research works and philosophy of science, modern political systems and political philosophy, scientific reasoning and its role in society, and key historical events of the past 75 years (Philosophy of Science, Contemporary World History, Political Philosophy, Liberal Arts and Science Education in the 21st Century)

Research methods, statistics and research training: Research Methods I and II, Introduction to Academic Skills, six concentration skills trainings (for example interviewing for academic research, systematic literature reviews, experimental methods) and research-oriented projects

Interdisciplinary liberal arts and sciences study: combining the social sciences, humanities and sciences, with general education outside the concentration and an optional interdisciplinary concentration, to investigate social and scientific problems from different perspectives
Social sciences domain: political science, international relations, international law, conflict studies, public policy and sociology, with quantitative and qualitative research methods
Humanities domain research: history and philosophy, with philosophical argument and analysis and research-based humanities projects such as documentaries

Natural sciences and sustainability: natural-science research, experimental methods and the sustainability and climate change direction as the scientific domain a social-science and humanities concentration studies alongside

Advanced concentration depth and independent research: a concentration with at least 20 EC of advanced courses over no fewer than three courses, advanced projects and a 20-EC Capstone research or analytical project
adjacent: Sciences domain and psychology: psychology, cognitive science and neuroscience, biomedical science and global health as concentration directions
Humanities domain: arts and literature, cultural studies and media studies as concentration directions, including research-based documentary work
Economics, business administration and international development as social-science concentration directions
Information and computer sciences and mathematics as science concentration directions
questions: How can complex social and scientific problems be investigated by combining academic disciplines and perspectives?
How do political systems, conflicts and the major historical events of recent decades shape contemporary societies?

studies human rights as positive law, in their history and in modern philosophy; it directly implements the international law direction and combines the legal and philosophical perspectives of the social-science and humanities domains

alternatives.label: Closest match to University College Maastricht: Interdisciplinary Social Sciences and Humanities with Research Methods and Sustainability
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum has seven political science, international relations and law courses (Foundations of Comparative Politics, Theory of International Relations, Peace & Conflict, European Union Politics, Law Society & Justice, Human Rights, Public International Law), four sociology courses, four philosophy and history courses forming the academic-core counterpart (Introduction to Western Philosophy, Modern History, Introduction to Political Philosophy, Ethics) plus two further history courses, three research-methods and data courses, two sustainability courses, one documentary-media course and Personal & Professional Development. It is therefore an interdisciplinary social-science and humanities programme with methods and sustainability, and not a single-field programme.
alternatives.concept: UCM has no single curriculum: every student takes the same academic core (philosophy of science, political philosophy, contemporary world history, liberal arts education), research methods, general education outside the chosen domain, a concentration with skills trainings and projects, and a Capstone, and the programme's own pages present combining the social sciences, humanities and natural sciences as its defining idea. The strongest defensible UCR response reproduces that structure as an interdisciplinary programme: UCR counterparts of the academic core in philosophy, history and political thought, research methods and statistics, a social-science and humanities concentration built from the political science, international relations, law, conflict, public policy and sociology directions that UCM lists, a documentary project, and natural-science and data courses as the general-education domain.
progression: Every formal prerequisite is scheduled in an earlier semester: Law, Society & Justice (semester 3) precedes Introduction to Public International Law (semester 4). Advisory progression is respected: the introductory philosophy, history, political philosophy and law courses are in semester 1, Introduction to Sociology and Modern Sociology (semester 3) precede New Issues in Contemporary Social Theory (semester 5), which builds on both, and the methods courses Research Methods & Statistics (semester 2) and Qualitative Research Methodology (semester 4) precede the research-oriented History Research Seminar and the other 300-level courses of semesters 5 and 6. Personal & Professional Development is in semester 2 of Year 1, because its availability and the 4-courses-per-semester pattern leave no room for it in semester 1.

alternatives.label: Mind, Brain and Health: Psychology, Cognitive Neuroscience and Biomedical Sciences
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum has eight psychology courses (Social Psychology, Statistics & Experimental Methods, Abnormal Psychology, Lifespan Developmental Psychology, Medical & Health Psychology, Advanced Research Seminar, Youth Resilience to Extremism, Psychodiagnostics & Psychotherapies), five cognitive science and neuroscience courses (including Philosophy of Mind), eight biomedical and life science courses, one public health course, the brain-and-behaviour gateway and Personal & Professional Development. It is therefore a sciences-domain programme on mind, brain and health spanning psychology, neuroscience and biomedicine, not a psychology-only or biomedicine-only programme.
alternatives.concept: UCM lists psychology, cognitive science and neuroscience, biomedical science and global health as stable study directions, and its sciences domain lets a student build a concentration around them. This alternative takes that direction as its organising logic instead of the interdisciplinary social-science and humanities core: a programme on how the brain, behaviour and the body produce health and illness, moving from the brain-and-behaviour and life-and-health gateways to psychology, cognitive neuroscience, physiology, pathology and public health, and ending with advanced seminars and a systematic-review methods course.
alternatives.distinctness: Alternative 1 is organised around the UCM academic core and a social-science and humanities concentration in politics, international relations, law and sociology, and has no psychology, neuroscience or biomedical course. Alternative 2 is organised around the sciences domain and psychology: it keeps only Personal & Professional Development and Statistics & Experimental Methods from Alternative 1 and replaces 22 of 24 courses with psychology, cognitive science, neuroscience, biomedical science and public health courses. The two programmes share 2 courses and each differs from the other by 22 courses (165 EC), well above the 30 EC / 4-course floor, and the differing courses follow directly from the change of organising direction, not from substitutions.
traceOverrides: teaches multivariate statistics including regression, factor analysis and ANOVA/ANCOVA for research on human behaviour and health; it directly implements the experimental and statistical research training of the psychology direction and is the methods foundation of the Advanced Research Seminar
progression: Every formal prerequisite is scheduled in an earlier semester: the gateways Introduction to Brain & Behavior and Foundation of Life, Health & Biomedicine (semester 1) precede every course that requires them, including Human Physiology and Higher Order Functions (semester 3), Abnormal Psychology (semester 4) and the 300-level biomedical and psychology courses of semesters 5 and 6. Advisory progression is respected: Higher Order Functions, which builds on introductory cognitive science, follows the gateway, Statistics & Experimental Methods (semester 3) precedes the Advanced Research Seminar (semester 6), and introductory psychology, neurobiology and cell biology come before the advanced psychology, pathology and pharmacology courses.

alternatives.label: Literature, Media, Art and Culture: Humanities with Philosophy and Communication
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum has six literature courses, six media studies courses (including The Documentary), four art history and archaeology courses, two communication and rhetoric courses, four philosophy and history courses and one qualitative methods course, together with Personal & Professional Development. It is therefore a humanities programme on literature, media, art and culture with philosophy and communication, not a literature-only programme.
alternatives.concept: UCM's humanities domain lists arts and literature, cultural studies, media studies, history and philosophy, and its projects include research-based documentaries. This alternative builds a humanities concentration around the arts and literature, cultural studies and media studies directions: how stories, images, films, media and public rhetoric produce and contest meaning in different cultures, supported by philosophy, history of gender, qualitative research methods and a documentary course.
alternatives.distinctness: Alternative 1 is a social-science and humanities programme organised around politics, law and sociology with a philosophy and history core; Alternative 2 is a sciences programme. Alternative 3 is organised around the humanities domain's arts and literature, cultural studies and media studies directions and keeps only Personal & Professional Development, Introduction to Western Philosophy, Ethics, Qualitative Research Methodology and The Documentary from Alternative 1. It shares 5 courses with Alternative 1 and 1 with Alternative 2, differs from Alternative 1 by 19 courses (142.5 EC) and from Alternative 2 by 23 courses (172.5 EC), and the differing courses follow from the change of organising direction to literature, media, art and culture.
traceOverrides: introduces central themes of Western philosophy and the theoretical methods philosophers use; it makes a specific complementary contribution as the philosophical foundation of the humanities concentration, alongside literary and cultural interpretation

teaches the main ethical theories and practical ethics including climate change and historical injustice; it makes a specific complementary contribution through the philosophical argument and analysis of the humanities domain

teaches qualitative research design and the interpretation of how people make sense of their world, and of how politics, history and cultures shape it; it directly supplies the interpretive research method for the cultural studies direction
traces the development of the documentary form and has students produce a short documentary; it directly implements media studies and the research-based documentary project UCM offers
progression: This alternative has no formal prerequisite. Advisory progression is respected: introductory literary studies, art history, film and media, rhetoric and archaeology (semesters 1 to 3) precede the 300-level Modern Art & Modern Museums, Film & Text, Media & Race, Persuasive Communication, Perspectives on Literary Meaning, Writing Art's Histories and Philosophy of Emotion (semesters 5 and 6), and Qualitative Research Methodology (semester 4) comes before the research-oriented seminars.

selection.assessment: Three UCR alternatives are defensible and the maximum was reached. UCM has no single curriculum: it is an interdisciplinary college whose students choose one of three domains, so the closest response (Alternative 1) is an interdisciplinary programme that reproduces the fixed UCM structure (academic core counterparts, research methods, general-education sciences and a social-science and humanities concentration). It owns fifteen generator-eligible rows: 6062 and 6063 (combining social sciences, humanities and natural sciences; investigating problems from different perspectives), 6064 to 6066 (social-science, humanities and natural-science research), 6068, 6071, 6072, 6073, 6075 and 6076 (conflict studies, international law, international relations, political science, public policy, sociology), 6077 (statistics and quantitative analysis), 6080 and 6082 (history, philosophy) and 6088 (sustainability and climate change), each implemented by courses in Alternative 1. Alternative 2 is built on the four sciences-domain and psychology directions 6074, 6083, 6084 and 6085 and Alternative 3 on the humanities directions 6078, 6079 and 6081; each shares at most 5 courses with another alternative (Alternative 1 and 2 share 2, Alternative 1 and 3 share 5, Alternative 2 and 3 share 1) and differs by at least 19 courses, so all pairs pass the 30 EC / 4-course floor. The remaining generator-eligible directions, business administration, economics and international development (6067, 6069, 6070) and information and computer science and mathematics (6086, 6087), are coherent and feasible candidates but were not needed once three alternatives were included: maximum-reached. Search-only outcome rows (6098 to 6110) and support-only curricular topics (6089 to 6097) did not generate any alternative.

blocks: Academic core: philosophy, history and political thought

Both address twentieth-century and recent world history; Modern History surveys 1815 to 2025 including the world wars, the Cold War and decolonisation, over a longer period than the past 75 years that Contemporary World History covers.

Both study political philosophy; Introduction to Political Philosophy examines influential Western thinkers on human nature, society and political authority and tests their theories against present problems, which is the subject of Political Philosophy in the UCM core.

Explicitly unmatched after semantic review: Philosophy of Science treats the epistemology of scientific inquiry; UCR has no philosophy-of-science course, and Introduction to Western Philosophy (which covers the nature of knowledge among many other themes) was not judged a direct counterpart.
Academic skills, methods and research training

Both develop core academic skills; Personal & Professional Development trains selecting and critically analysing sources, articulating research questions and arguments and academic writing, which is the educational function of an introduction to academic skills, although UCM's component is a 2.5-EC skills training.

Explicitly unmatched after semantic review: Liberal Arts and Science Education in the 21st Century reflects on the nature of liberal arts education; Personal & Professional Development concerns personal formation and academic skills and is matched to the academic-skills component instead.

Both are introductions to research methods; Research Methods & Statistics covers research design, operationalisation, sampling and descriptive and inferential statistics, which is an important and identifiable part of introductory research-methods training, although UCM's skills training content is not published.

Explicitly unmatched after semantic review: Research Methods II is a 2.5-EC skills training whose content is not published on a readable page; no UCR course was judged a specific counterpart beyond the introductory methods course already matched.
Explicitly unmatched after semantic review: Introduction to Academic Skills II is a 7.5-EC first-year project; UCR has no corresponding project course in the scheduled curriculum.
Explicitly unmatched after semantic review: the Research Project is a 5-EC first-year project; no scheduled UCR course is a project of that kind.

Explicitly unmatched after semantic review: the six concentration skills trainings are individual choices (for example interviewing and systematic reviews) that the sources do not name, so no UCR course can be matched to them as a group.

Explicitly unmatched after semantic review: the three concentration projects are individual choices of three-week projects, internships or research projects that the sources do not name, so no UCR course can be matched to them as a group.
Political science, international relations and law
Biomedical and life sciences and public health

Explicitly unmatched after semantic review: general education is an individual restricted choice of three courses outside the concentration domain that the sources do not name; the UCR programmes spread their courses across domains differently and no single course corresponds to it.

Explicitly unmatched after semantic review: the fifteen concentration courses depend on the domain the student chooses and are not named in the sources; the UCR concentration-like course groups appear in the blocks above without being forced onto this open component.

Explicitly unmatched after semantic review: the 20-EC Capstone is an individual advanced research or analytical project; UCR has no scheduled Capstone course, and the standardized optional independent research element is shown against this component.

notes.text: University College Maastricht organizes study around a fixed academic core, general education, a concentration chosen in the social sciences, humanities or sciences (or an interdisciplinary mix), skills trainings, projects and a Capstone. At UCR, comparable subjects are distributed across courses in political science, law, sociology, philosophy, history, psychology, neuroscience, biomedical science, literature and media. The UCR programmes therefore cover related territory through a different curricular structure rather than reproducing the UCM programme component by component, and each UCR alternative stands for one possible concentration route.

Both programmes include substantial study of philosophy, history, political thought and research methods in the first years. The UCM core additionally includes Philosophy of Science, Liberal Arts and Science Education in the 21st Century, project modules and a 20-EC Capstone. UCR students can instead combine courses from the Government & Society, Health, Cognition & Behavior and Media, Culture & Communication clusters, but those components are not offered as separate courses.
